title: Manchonack / Gardiners Island
summary: Manchonack is Tooker's placename for Gardiners Island in East Hampton. The name appears in the 1639 deed by Yovawan, sachem of Pommanocc, and Aswaw to Lion Gardiner. The name is interpreted as a land of the departed.
address_label: Gardiners Island, East Hampton, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point placed on the southern interior of Gardiners Island so the Manchonack marker sits on land and remains separated from the Montaukett ancestral land label; not a deed boundary or precise historic coordinate.
translation_content:
The name Manchonack is interpreted through forms meaning a place where many people had died or land of the departed. This is connected with Montaukett oral tradition of a severe sickness before English settlement and with Algonquian words for those who have gone or departed.

Why Place Names Matter

“When a name is meaningless there is a tendency to alter it to something else which does mean something.”

— Henry Cecil Wyld and T. Oakes Hirst, The Place Names of Lancashire (1911), Internet Archive scan leaf 207
land_loss_content: Manchonack links Gardiners Island to Montaukett memory, epidemic history, and one of the earliest English land transactions in eastern Long Island. The name preserves an Indigenous explanation of the island that differs sharply from later colonial ownership names.
whereintheworld_content: The map outlines modern Gardiners Island, the place identified in the 1639 deed as Manchonat. The shoreline shown is modern and should not be read as a reconstruction of the island's 1639 shoreline or the full deeded area.
